title: Board Policy on Multiple Construction Projects and the Allowance of Each Project (Line Extensions and New Service Construction)
content:
**Section 1 — One project per location.** Under Line Extensions and New Service Construction, a member of Cedar Fork Electric Cooperative may have several construction projects, one per location to be served; a farm may extend to a home, a bin site and a pivot as separate projects. No limit is set on the number of projects one member may hold: the count follows the locations to be served.

**Section 2 — Allowance stays with its project.** Each project's allowance belongs to that project only: where the class of extension does not allow an unused allowance to be moved to another project, footage or revenue allowance unused on one project is never moved to another.

## The two sections restated

| Question the policy answers | Answer under this policy |
|---|---|
| How many projects may one member have? | Several, one per location to be served, with no set maximum. |
| What is one project? | The construction for one location to be served. |
| Whose allowance is it? | The project's own. |
| Can footage or revenue allowance unused on one project be put toward another, where the class does not allow an unused allowance to be moved? | No, never. |

## Illustration (hypothetical farm member)

A hypothetical farm member asks for power at three locations on the home place: a new farmhouse, a grain bin site and an irrigation pivot. These are three separate construction projects, each with its own application and its own allowance under its own class. Suppose the farmhouse project leaves part of its footage allowance unused because the house sits close to the existing line, and the class does not allow an unused allowance to be moved. That unused footage stays with the farmhouse project; it is not moved to the bin site project or to the pivot project, each of which is estimated on its own allowance alone.
